source_caption:
Often called one of the greatest films ever made, A Brighter Summer Day(1991) is Edward Yang’s masterful portrait of youth and growing up in 1960s Taipei. The film follows a group of teenagers navigating friendship, family, and identity during a time of quiet social tension.

Told with patience and remarkable sensitivity, the film finds meaning in small moments and unspoken emotions. Edward Yang’s careful observation turns everyday life into something profound, making A Brighter Summer Day a deeply moving and enduring masterpiece.

If you haven’t watched it yet, it’s absolutely worth experiencing.

source_details.synopsis: A Brighter Summer Day is a 1991 Taiwanese epic crime drama film directed by Edward Yang, associated with the New Taiwanese Cinema. Its English title is derived from the lyrics of Elvis Presley's 1960 rendition of "Are You Lonesome Tonight?". Set in the late 1950s and early '60s, the film centers on Hsiao Si’r (Chang Chen), a boy from a middle-class home who veers into juvenile delinquency. The film was selected as the Taiwanese entry for the Best Foreign Language Film at the 64th Academy Awards but was not nominated.
